content.thinking:
I'm tracing the causal chain: account page errors spiked due to a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py, triggered when a feature flag started evaluating as on around 14:54, and I'm now digging into why that flag change caused the division error in the monthly calculation.

I'm ruling out deploys as a cause since the deploy records show nothing came back in the relevant window, and the only production change was the admin flipping the flag — confirmed by reverting it restoring service. The pre-existing ClientDisconnected errors look like unrelated background noise since they predate onset with otherwise healthy metrics.

Now I'm pinning down the actual bug: the average_spend_per_item_this_month calculation divides by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who haven't bought anything yet this month.

The flag seems to have gone to full traffic within a minute with no staged percentage rollout — that's a real contributing factor, so I'll propose rolling out flags by percentage with an automatic error-rate gate. As for the lack of an on-call page, since mitigation already happened in two minutes, paging wouldn't have sped things up, so I'll skip that and also skip commenting on alert detection speed since nothing ties flag toggles to error-rate monitoring.

For action items: AI-3 is to enable the monthly-spend feature via staged rollout that halts on error spikes (a prevent item), and AI-4 is to require flag-on test coverage for flag-gated code paths as a review process before enabling flags. I'm also considering whether to add an item blocking re-enabling the flag until the fix in PR #323 merges, since leaving it off doesn't fully protect against the same failure recurring.

For lessons learned, what went well was that Argus detected the issue and reverted the flag promptly after the alert, restoring service. What went wrong is that no on-call person was actually paged despite the alert firing, and the flag had been switched on by an admin without proper staging.

As for luck, I don't think there's a strong case here — the fact that the flag change was the only change in the window made it easier to diagnose, but I shouldn't overreach calling that luck, so I'll leave it empty. The real risk still outstanding is that the division-by-zero bug remains unfixed in the code, so re-enabling monthly-spend-feature before a proper fix would cause account pages to fail again for the same shoppers.

The root cause: enabling monthly-spend-feature routes account page rendering through a calculation that divides this month's total spend by this month's purchase count, and for shoppers with zero purchases this month, that count is zero, triggering a ZeroDivisionError and failing the page — though I should note this is based on a code reading, not a confirmed test. Contributing factors include no staged rollout (it went to all evaluations within a minute) and no test coverage for the flag-on path with zero monthly purchases, which ties to addressing AI-2 and AI-4. I should flag that the affected-shopper estimate is itself inferred from code reading rather than measured data.

I'm ruling out deploys as a cause since no deploys occurred the day before the incident except the flag flip itself, and the service was confirmed healthy on its existing revision before onset, which rules out earlier changes as the trigger — though revision convergence data only confirms state after the fact, not continuous health.

I can also rule out the ClientDisconnected errors since they occurred well before onset (14:25-14:55) and had stopped by the time the real incident started, confirming they're unrelated background noise.

action_items.item: Turn monthly-spend-feature (and future flags like it) on through a staged percentage rollout that stops itself if the account page error rate rises.
Before a feature flag can be switched on in production, require tests that run its code path with the flag on, including the case of a shopper with past purchases but none this month.
Block monthly-spend-feature from being switched back on until the fix proposed in PR #323 is merged and deployed.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests failed for shoppers. The share of all requests answered with a server error rose from {series_before} before the onset to {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, peaking at {series_at_worst}. So a sizeable share of shoppers opening their account page got an error instead of the page.
From the onset, account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. None came back in the day before the onset; the only production change read was the flag switch.

Any earlier change already in place. Before the onset the service ran healthy with the flag off: the error rate was near its usual level and account pages rendered normally. It recovered once only the flag was reverted, with everything else left in place.
Shoppers closing the connection (ClientDisconnected). These errors were already logged throughout the healthy stretch before the onset, so they are background and not the cause.

causal_chain.step: The monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on by admin at {P1.1}. That sent account page requests down the monthly spend-summary code path. Flag evaluations went from all off before the onset to partly on in the onset minute and then all on. Reverting only this flag brought the service back, and the action was confirmed.

On the monthly path, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases marked as this month. Per Code-Fix's reading of the source (unverified; nothing ran it), that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, so the division raises at line 47. The logged ZeroDivisionError at that line matches this reading.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through a calculation that divides by zero, so those pages failed; a reading of the code that nothing has tested says this happens for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for all account page traffic within about a minute. No staged percentage rollout and no check of the error rate as it went out were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A small staged share of traffic would have hit the error first. The rollout could have been stopped before most shoppers' account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that runs the flag-on monthly path for a shopper with no purchases this month. Per Code-Fix, the existing tests cover only the lifetime path, and its new tests raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a test would have failed before the flag was switched on, which would have shown the division by zero ahead of production.

went_well: Argus reverted the monthly-spend-feature flag {T18.1 - T1.1} after receiving the alert, acting on the leading candidate without waiting for a person.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed the revert {T21.1 - T18.1} after making it, by seeing the service leave the incident's level.
Because the investigation read the flag provider's history and the production change events together, the flag switch stood out as the only change, and no deploy was involved.
went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was brought in.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, account page requests go through `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, which divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases made this month. Where that number is zero, the code raises ZeroDivisionError at line 47 and the request fails. The logs show the ZeroDivisionError at that line. That the count is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month comes only from Code-Fix's reading of the source, which nothing has run.
input.still_at_risk: The division by zero is still in the code, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place would make account pages fail again in the same way.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
